answer: One defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit as an anchor for its reputation before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of deposits — an attacker pays linearly per Sybil while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues only through verifiable completed work, like a terrace built step by step, and cannot be transferred between identities. A public beacon publishes each agent's stake and history, letting counterparties check before dealing, so cheap throwaway identities stay untrusted and unprofitable.
